title: Chlamydia, inflammation, and atherogenesis.
text_summary: 动脉粥样硬化病变的发生和进展主要是由于慢性纤维增殖性炎症反应。这篇综述讨论了肺炎衣原体如何可能导致这种慢性炎症反应，并报告了最近的体内和体外研究。小鼠体内研究表明，肺炎衣原体感染通过肺泡巨噬细胞感染肺部后传播到动脉壁。最近的体外研究表明，受感染的U937细胞可以直接将感染转移至内皮细胞，并可以间接增加内皮细胞对肺炎衣原体感染的易感性。用修饰形式的低密度脂蛋白加载RAW 264.7细胞增加了细胞对肺炎衣原体感染的抵抗力，并且还增加了对修饰脂质和肺炎衣原体感染的联合毒性作用的敏感性。

Chlamydia, Inﬂammation, and Atherogenesis

Michael E. Rosenfeld, Erwin Blessing, Tsun Mei Lin,                                            Department of Pathobiology,
Teresa C. Moazed, Lee Ann Campbell,                                                                University of Washington, Seattle
and Cho-chou Kuo


                    Atherosclerotic lesions are initiated and progress largely as a result of a chronic, ﬁbropro-
                     liferative, inﬂammatory response. This review discusses how Chlamydia pneumoniae could
                 conceivably contribute to this chronic inﬂammatory response and reports on recent in vivo
              and in vitro studies. In vivo studies in mice demonstrate that C. pneumoniae infection is
                disseminated to the artery wall following infection in the lung by alveolar macrophages.Recent
                  in vitro studies show that infected U937 cells can directly transfer infection to endothelial
                     cells and can indirectly increase the susceptibility of endothelial cells to C. pneumoniae infec-
                   tion. Loading of RAW 264.7 cells with modiﬁed forms of low-density lipoprotein increases
                 the resistance of the cells to C. pneumoniae infection and also increases the susceptibility to
                 the combined toxic effects of modiﬁed lipids and C. pneumoniae infection.
